fields.label: Event story
fields.sample:
Exactly thirty years ago, on a March morning, the family’s most cheerful member came into the world. Ever since, every room gets a little brighter and every table gets an extra laugh.
This paper is a small tribute to those thirty years — and a fine excuse to raise our glasses tonight in celebration.

fields.label: Thank-you message
fields.sample: Thank you for sharing this evening with us and for your generous good wishes. Here’s to many more happy years, together!

elements.name: Haber başlığı
elements.text: The family’s most cheerful member arrived one sunny morning, and joy overflowed

elements.name: Haber metni
elements.text:
Ac­cord­ing to hos­pi­tal sources, the baby is healthy, cheer­ful and con­sid­er­ably louder than ex­pect­ed. We have learned that the father, who paced the ma­ter­ni­ty cor­ri­dor until dawn, handed out candy to the whole floor the moment he heard the news, while the grand­moth­er never once left the phone.
The nurses on duty said the new­born was hand­ing out smiles from the very first hours, and the ward soon turned into a full-blown cel­e­bra­tion. Family friends agree that the baby has Mom’s eyes and Dad’s de­ter­mi­na­tion. The first ques­tion from Grand­pa, wait­ing at the door, was “Who does the baby look like?” The answer is still being debated.
Experts pre­dict this cheer­ful­ness will not fade over the years; on the con­trary, it will grow a little with every birth­day. Our paper will keep fol­low­ing de­vel­op­ments close­ly and will report them on this page every year.

elements.name: Kısa haber
elements.text: The neigh­bors’ Turk­ish de­light ran out by noon; the corner shop or­dered more.

elements.name: Kısa haber
elements.text: After a lengthy family meet­ing, ev­ery­one agreed on the very first name sug­gest­ed.

elements.name: Kısa haber
elements.text: Grand­pa brought a box of col­ored pen­cils and said, “May your life be col­or­ful.”

elements.name: Kısa haber
elements.text: Clear skies all day, a light breeze and a 100 per­cent chance of joy.

elements.name: Sayfa manşeti
elements.text: What was the world up to that year?

elements.name: Spot
elements.text: A historic defeat on the chessboard, first pictures from Mars, a giant iceberg on the big screen… This is what the papers wrote the year they were born.

elements.name: Haber başlığı
elements.text: A historic day at the chessboard: computer beats world champion

elements.name: Haber metni
elements.text:
At the end of a six-game match in New York, IBM’s Deep Blue com­put­er de­feat­ed world chess cham­pi­on Garry Kas­parov. It was the first time a ma­chine had beaten a reign­ing world cham­pi­on in a match under clas­si­cal time con­trols, and the result sent shock­waves through the sci­en­tif­ic world.
The au­di­ence pack­ing the hall held its breath during the final game. After the match, Kas­parov said he found some of the computer’s moves “too human”; ex­perts agreed that the door had opened to a new age in which ma­chines learn to think.
Our chess colum­nist noted that read­ers who saw the news asked cof­fee­hous­es for chess­boards in­stead of backgam­mon that evening, but most gave up after the first move and went back to rolling dice.

elements.name: Alıntı
elements.text: “We laughed when they said machines would play chess one day. Now we argue about who will beat whom.”

elements.name: Kısa haber
elements.text: The Pathfind­er probe landed on Mars in July; the little rover So­journ­er ex­am­ined the red planet’s rocks one by one.

elements.name: Kısa haber
elements.text: In Feb­ru­ary, Scot­tish sci­en­tists in­tro­duced the world to the first mammal cloned from an adult cell.

elements.name: Kısa haber
elements.text: In a cer­e­mo­ny on the first day of July, Hong Kong was handed over to China after more than a cen­tu­ry and a half of British rule.

elements.name: Kısa haber
elements.text: Comet Hale-Bopp was vis­i­ble to the naked eye all spring; bal­conies turned into night­time ob­ser­va­to­ries.

elements.name: Kısa haber
elements.text: A young author’s first novel, “Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone,” was pub­lished in London in June. Nobody guessed how beloved it would become.

elements.name: Kısa haber
elements.text: Re­leased in De­cem­ber, Ti­tan­ic quick­ly smashed box-office records; tissue sales out­side the­aters rose too.

elements.name: Kısa haber
elements.text: Tarkan’s “Şı­marık” never left the air­waves; the chorus with its kiss­ing sound soon crossed bor­ders.

elements.name: Kısa haber
elements.text: DVD play­ers that fit whole movies on a thin disc went on sale; video­tapes are wor­ried.

elements.text: Mom recalls: “No crying on day one, only laughter”

elements.name: Soru
elements.text: — What did the baby do first?

elements.name: Cevap
elements.text: — No tears, just giggles. Even the nurses were amazed.

elements.name: Soru
elements.text: — What did the baby love most?

elements.name: Cevap
elements.text: — Music. Turn on the radio and those little feet would dance.

elements.name: Cevap
elements.text: — Trying to trim the cat’s whiskers with Dad’s mustache scissors.

elements.name: Cevap
elements.text: — Just keep smiling like this; the rest will follow.

elements.name: Okur mektubu
elements.text: Dear Editor, after read­ing the birth an­nounce­ment, I took two sugars in my morn­ing tea. I wish the baby and the family a life­time of hap­pi­ness, and I hope your paper never runs short of such lovely news. I will read it to my grand­chil­dren too.

elements.text: The best news of a lifetime

elements.name: Spot
elements.text: From first steps to first paycheck, from the first day of school to tonight: a life, year by year, frame by frame.

elements.name: Not 0
elements.text: Laughing, not crying — or so the family says.

elements.name: Not 1
elements.text: Three steps from rug to coffee table. The applause still echoes.

elements.name: Not 7

elements.name: Not 12
elements.text: A scar on the knee, a huge smile on the face.

elements.name: Not 18

elements.name: Not 22
elements.text: Cap in the air, dreams up ahead.

elements.name: Not 25
elements.text: Bought Mom a gift with the first paycheck.

elements.name: Kare 2 altyazı
elements.text: A summer evening with friends: laughter never ran short.

elements.name: Kare 3 altyazı
elements.text: Every birthday: the same table, the same candles, always new wishes.

elements.name: Söz
elements.text: “No one in class laughed more; before long, even the teachers would start laughing.”

elements.name: Söz
elements.text: “Impossible to keep a secret from them; but their secrets are safe with us.”

elements.name: Söz
elements.text: “One call and they’re here; two laughs and the night is saved.”

elements.text: This story from the archives also heralds a celebration. We would be delighted to have you join us.

elements.name: Program notu 21.30

elements.name: Parti altyazısı
elements.text: Dance floor ready, music ready; all that’s missing is you.

elements.name: Arka fotoğraf altyazısı
elements.text: The best shot of the night: friends, raised glasses and endless laughter.

elements.name: Dilek
elements.text: “The best part of all these years: your laughter was in every one.”

elements.name: Dilek
elements.text: “Growing up with you was a gift; growing old with you will be too.”

elements.name: Dilek
elements.text: “The biggest slice of cake is always yours.”

elements.name: Dilek
elements.text: “Many happy returns; may each new year be better than the last.”

elements.text: Tonight, you’ll raise the first glass.

elements.name: Burç yorumu Boğa

elements.name: Burç yorumu İkizler

elements.name: Burç yorumu Aslan

elements.name: Burç yorumu Başak

elements.name: Burç yorumu Terazi
elements.text: A tough choice between appetizers and dessert.

elements.name: Burç yorumu Akrep
elements.text: You know the childhood secrets; keep them.

elements.name: Burç yorumu Yay
elements.text: The night’s longest dance is yours.

elements.name: Burç yorumu Kova
elements.text: New friendships will form at the table.

elements.name: Burç yorumu Balık
elements.text: The old songs may bring tears to your eyes.

elements.name: Köşe yazısı
elements.text: Every birth­day is like an old news­pa­per pulled from the ar­chives: the pages may yellow, but the news never gets old. Every glass raised tonight re­prints the joy of that very first morn­ing. Before blow­ing out the can­dles, pause for a moment and think back on the years gone by; the best head­lines have yet to be writ­ten.

elements.name: İlan metni
elements.text: Last seen last summer. Finders need not return it; we’re happy as we are.

elements.name: İlan metni
elements.text: Timeless songs, endless conversations, shoulders to lean on through every trouble. Not negotiable.

elements.name: İlan metni
elements.text: Volunteers wanted who can blow out every candle on the cake in one breath.

elements.name: İlan metni
elements.text: The birthday star may not be contradicted tonight; every wish will be granted.

elements.name: İlan metni
elements.text: A roomy space that clears out after midnight, where taking off your shoes is allowed.

elements.name: İlan metni
elements.text: Heartfelt thanks to everyone who has lit our way up to this day.
